E-LEARNING WEBINARS
e-learning webinars cover a variety of topics on U.S. and international education. Our e-learning webinars are designed to help international admissions professionals, recruiters, credential evaluators, state regulatory/licensing board examiners, human resource administrators, students and international candidates understand the U.S. educational system and academic credentials from around the world as well as trends and developments in education and learning.
ACEI’s e-learning webinars include both lecture and interactive components designed to provide attendees with practical take-away tools. Our e-learning webinars are facilitated and taught by our experienced senior evaluation staff as well as guest educators from academic institutions and organizations engaged in international admissions and enrollment, curriculum development and instruction and comparative education.

The Rise of Human-Centric Skills (in the world of AI)
In a world driven by rapid technological advancements and the growing influence of AI, the importance of human-centric skills has never been greater. This webinar invites you to explore how qualities like emotional intelligence, adaptability, creativity, and collaboration are redefining the future of work amidst concerns about job security in the age of AI. We will consider why organizations are prioritizing these uniquely human attributes to drive innovation, build strong workplace cultures, and navigate the complexities of a rapidly changing environment alongside AI’s capabilities. Additionally, we will examine the current limitations of AI and how they highlight the increasing demand for human-centric skills that remain irreplaceable in today’s evolving workforce.
Presenter: Alistair Bell Wylie

The Education System of Scotland
Scotland has a long and proud history of education but it is a system which stands alone from the rest of the UK. This webinar aims to give an overview and history of the education system of Scotland looking at the main sectors, national curriculum and qualifications. A useful piece of learning for those who are not familiar with Scottish education.

Finding the Right Fit University (Session One)
The
Finding the Right Fit University
webinar is aimed at helping students navigate the college search process. It covers various aspects such as academic programs, campus culture, extracurricular activities, and financial aid options. The webinar provides valuable insights and tips on how to identify universities that align with your interests, goals, and values. It also offers guidance on researching and evaluating potential schools, making informed decisions, and ultimately finding the perfect fit for your higher education journey. Whether you’re a high school student or a transfer student, this webinar is designed to assist you in finding the university that best suits your needs.
Presenter: Dmitry Satsuk
Click here
Applying to Colleges and Universities in the U.S. (Session Two)
The
Applying to Colleges and Universities in the United States
webinar is a comprehensive session aimed at providing students with guidance and support throughout the college application process. It covers various aspects such as creating a strong application, writing compelling essays, securing strong letters of recommendation, and preparing for standardized tests like the SAT or ACT. The webinar also offers valuable insights into the different application requirements and deadlines for various universities, as well as strategies for maximizing your chances of acceptance. Whether you’re an international student or a domestic student, this webinar is designed to help you navigate the complex and competitive process of applying to universities in the United States. It provides valuable tips and resources to ensure that you submit a strong and well-rounded application that highlights your unique strengths and accomplishments.
Presenter: Dmitry Satsuk
Click here
Financial Aid for International Student (Session Three)
The
Financial Aid for International Students
webinar is a helpful session specifically designed to provide information and guidance on the various financial aid opportunities available to international students studying in the United States. The webinar covers topics such as scholarships, grants, loans, and work-study programs that can help offset the cost of tuition, living expenses, and other educational costs. It also provides insights into the application process for financial aid, including tips on how to search for scholarships and grants, how to write a compelling financial aid essay, and how to navigate the complex financial aid application forms. The webinar aims to equip international students with the knowledge and resources they need to make informed decisions about financing their education in the United States, ultimately helping them pursue their academic goals with financial support.
Presenter: Dmitry Satsuk

Micro-credentials – new concept or just a re-invention?
Micro-credentials have recently gained prominence in education circles. Are they really something new? Or just a re-invention of an old concept? There are lots of questions surrounding micro-credentials, not least of which surround their value and relevance. Whilst they may provide some interesting solutions for students looking for flexibility, there are wider questions about their relevance and value which are of interest to those of us in the world of credential evaluation.

International higher education institutions are those
that
